question: Can the public stdio relay route cancellation and supervised Win32 release while its actual child-process stdout OS pipe is full and a write is blocked?
scope: One synthetic owned Win32 fixture. Relay child uses actual subprocess stdin/stdout pipes; its MCP server/session transport is an in-process adapter. No GZDoom, MAP01, WSLc, Docker, provider, model, efficiency, or reliability claim.

frozen_conditions.fixture: Fresh runtime.backends.win32_v1.fixture_app process and exact HWND only; never attach to or control an existing application.
frozen_conditions.action: Public interface_dispatch through runtime.cli_v1.mcp_relay: focus exact fixture, SHIFT down, wait_update 8000 ms, SHIFT up, release_all.
frozen_conditions.stdout_pressure: Stop parent reads after setup, send sixteen ordinary interface_observe calls, one ordinary interface_clock call, then standard interface_cancel for the exact dispatch call.
frozen_conditions.blocked_pipe_evidence: Before any stdout drain, require PeekNamedPipe buffered bytes >= GetNamedPipeInfo outbound capacity, a writer write_started without a corresponding write_completed, server-side interface_cancel_returned, and independent exact-generation native SHIFT-up.
frozen_conditions.success: All blocked-pipe gate conditions hold before drain; after drain, retained exact-call result says cancellation status recovered and release_confirmed true, with same target generation and independent SHIFT-up.
frozen_conditions.failure: Any unmet/ambiguous gate is retained as the first FAIL_OR_UNKNOWN outcome; never replay the attempt. Emergency release may be used only on the owned fixture and must be recorded.
frozen_conditions.retention: Save full result, raw fixture/relay logs, pipe observations and SHA256SUMS under run/ before reporting.

operator_boundary: Run only on this Windows PC and only against the newly started fixture. Do not launch, focus, or input to GZDoom or any pre-existing process in this attempt.
preflight: Both Python modules compile; source hashes frozen before first fixture or input action.
